profile.goal: improve posture, reduce lower back stiffness, build a movement habit
profile.equipment: long loop resistance band, mini glute band, floor space, sturdy dining chair
profile.injuries_notes: mild lower back ache after sitting, no sharp pain; eases up with standing/walking, hasn't traveled into hip or leg
profile.schedule: 3 days/week, max 30 min/session, non-consecutive days preferred, mid-morning ideal

vineeth.current_plan:
Thank you for sharing all that — it paints a really clear picture, and it's all encouraging news! 🙌 The fact that your back eases up with movement (and hasn't traveled into your hip or leg) is a great sign that gentle, consistent movement is exactly the right medicine here. And a "fresh start" is a beautiful thing — your body remembers being active from your sports days, so you may surprise yourself!

Two small things I want to gently flag for your success:
- **Sleep is your #1 recovery tool.** 6-7 inconsistent hours can absolutely contribute to afternoon fog *and* muscle stiffness. Even nudging toward a consistent bedtime will amplify everything we do. No pressure to fix it overnight — just something to keep an eye on. 😊
- **Timing matters for you.** Since you're sharpest mid-morning, that could be your ideal workout window if your schedule allows. Movement then may also help fight that late-afternoon fog!

Here's my suggestion: **schedule your 3 sessions on non-consecutive days** (like Mon/Wed/Fri) so your body gets recovery time. Pair that with those hourly stand-and-move breaks, and you're building a rock-solid foundation.

Ready to lock in your start day? **Which day this week would you like to tackle Day 1** — and would a mid-morning slot work for you? 💪
